answer: Aging-cost identity throttle: each new identity starts with a low daily action ceiling that rises only with continuous, verifiable participation. Like a rising tide, the ceiling lifts slowly, so launching many identities at once yields little throughput. A fable can be published on day one; influence cannot. Costs are real: to match one mature identity an attacker must fund many young ones and pay their ongoing compute, monitoring, and yarrow-thin margins for months before any cohort reaches useful capacity, while anomaly detection culls early.
